conviction_note: The numbers are new and nothing was pre-released, and a narrowing of the revenue guide is plausible, so abs_move is 7.0 (this name's observed release-day median is about 5.9%). p_up is 47: a mild negative lean from guide arithmetic (FY consensus of EUR 2.40bn needs about a +33% y/y Q4) and from free cash flow, offset by strong counterparty order data, supervisory-board buying into the print and a stock already 27% off its September high with 4.3% disclosed short. The findings sum to -1.0 and the scaled number is -0.42. The scaled number is smaller because p_up is held near 50: the negatives are inferences from public numbers, and the drawdown may already price a low-end narrowing.

findings.finding: FY26 revenue consensus (FactSet, 7 analysts) is EUR 2,399m, the guidance midpoint. With H1 at EUR 1,115.3m and Q3 consensus at EUR 560.1m, that implies a Q4 of about EUR 724m against EUR 543.4m in Q4 2025 (+33% y/y, +24% on Q2's EUR 585m). The release is therefore likely to narrow revenue toward the lower half, as Deutz did with its 9M 2025 statement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 9M 2025 (2025-11-06): revenue guided to the low end (about EUR 2.1bn), stock -1.3%. FY guide on 2026-03-26 disappointed: -7.2% on the day (up to -9% intraday, per Börsen-Zeitung). H1 2026 confirmation: +3.3%, then +2.9% the next day.
findings.original_quote: Quartalsschätzungen Umsatzerlöse ... letztes Quartal zum 30.09.2026 ... Anzahl Analysten 3 ... Mittlere Schätzung 560,07 ... aktuelles Geschäftsjahr zum 31.12.2026 ... 7 ... 2.399,19 (Quelle: FactSet). In English: quarterly revenue estimates, quarter to 30.09.2026, 3 analysts, mean estimate 560.07; current fiscal year to 31.12.2026, 7 analysts, 2,399.19.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the implied Q4 arithmetic. If the market held the consensus number, the FY revenue mean would have moved below the guidance midpoint as the stock fell 27% from its September high. It has not, so either the estimates are stale or a low-end narrowing would still lower them. Some of this may already sit in the drawdown, which is why the finding is capped small.
findings.independence: The 9M 2025 precedent of a low-end narrowing (https://rermag.com/news-analysis/headline-news/article/55328808/deutz-jumps-first-nine-months-revenue-149-percent-with-help-from-acquisitions); reports of small-engine weakness (https://www.finanztrends.de/news/deutz-aktie-stellenabbau-belastet-kurs/)

findings.finding: Counterparties that reported Q3 2026 show strong construction-equipment demand. Volvo CE: orders +16%, deliveries +8%, organic machine sales +13%, with market growth in every region including Europe. Caterpillar Construction Industries: sales +18%. Q3 orders also face an easy comparison (Q3 2025 EUR 470.4m, -15% y/y), and Warburg and MPCM expect a clear rise in Q3 orders.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 orders +41%: stock +4.7%. H1 2026 orders +28.7%: +3.3%, then +2.9% the next day. 9M 2025 Q3 orders -15%: -1.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the analysts' expectation of strong orders is in German preview copy. The stock nonetheless fell from 10.72 to 9.72 after Volvo CE (23 Oct) and Caterpillar (29 Oct) reported, so the peer read-through has not lifted it. If it were priced, DEZ would have tracked the CE peers higher.
findings.independence: Caterpillar Q3 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000018230/000001823026000052/ex991toformcat3q2026earnin.htm); Warburg's order view, in German (https://www.kapitalmarktexperten.de/deutz-aktie-stellenabbau-oder-auftraege/)

findings.finding: Handelsblatt (6 Oct) reported up to 400 job cuts in the small-engine business at Cologne-Porz because of weaker demand, and a Deutz spokesman confirmed talks with employee representatives. That points to Engines softness in Q3 and a likely restructuring charge in exceptional items, below adj. EBIT.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Exceptional items have not moved prior prints visibly: the 2025 Future Fit charges came with positive adj. EBIT reactions (+12.1% on 2025-08-07).
findings.original_quote: Laut Handelsblatt könnten am Kölner Stammwerk bis zu 400 Stellen wegfallen; rund 100 Arbeitsplätze seien bereits abgebaut oder befinden sich im Abbau. Ein Unternehmenssprecher bestätigte dazu laufende Verhandlungen mit den Arbeitnehmervertretern. In English: according to Handelsblatt, up to 400 jobs could go at the Cologne headquarters plant; about 100 had already been cut or were being cut. A company spokesman confirmed ongoing negotiations with employee representatives.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public since 6-7 Oct, when the stock fell. What is not priced is the size of the charge and how much small-engine weakness shows up in Engines' Q3 margin, which only the release shows. The size is small and negative because this is a one-off below adj. EBIT, and the operating signal is only inferred.
findings.independence: Kion's Q3 2026 orders fell 0.9% y/y (a forklift OEM, not confirmed as a Deutz account) (https://www.kiongroup.com/KION-Website-Main/Investor-Relations/Reports-Presentations/2026-Reports-Presentations/Q3-2026/2026-Q3_Quartalsmitteilung_KION.pdf)

findings.finding: H1 2026 FCF before M&A was EUR -29.7m, with operating cash flow down to EUR 31.9m on an inventory build. The FY guide of FCF before M&A in the high double-digit millions needs roughly EUR +100m or more in H2, and a Q4-loaded revenue plan argues for more inventory in Q3. A trimmed FCF guide or a weak 9M cash flow is a real risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior on FCF alone at Deutz. At Luceco, FCF from an inventory build outweighed a raised guide (-5.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 number is public, but the FY FCF guide has not been revised, and finanzen.net's FY26 operating cash flow consensus of EUR 180.7m implies estimates still assume a strong H2. A cut would be new information on the line where this release adds most beyond the quarter.
findings.independence: FactSet FY26 operating cash flow consensus of EUR 180.7m (https://www.finanzen.net/schaetzungen/deutz)

findings.finding: Supervisory-board members and a closely associated person bought DEUTZ shares inside the 30 days before the print: Helmut Ernst EUR 99.6k at 9.96 (22 Oct), Dr. Dietmar Voggenreiter EUR 50.4k plus Dr. Simone Voggenreiter about EUR 99k (22 Oct), and Melanie Freytag EUR 48.2k at 9.64 (30 Oct, the day of the -7.1% drop). All at about 15-18% below the September ABB price of EUR 11.70.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insiders bought repeatedly before past prints (March, August, September 2026); results-day reactions were mixed (+4.7%, +3.3%, -7.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: The buys are public on EQS, but the stock kept falling after them (9.96 on 22 Oct, 9.44 on 30 Oct). The amounts are small, so the size stays small.

findings.finding: The 30 Oct drop (-7.1% on 1.76m shares, the heaviest volume of the month) coincided with a WirtschaftsWoche report that the Bundeswehr ZEBEL spare-parts software failure could put about 150 FFG staff on short-time work. FFG is not yet consolidated (closing expected end-2026/early-2027), so it cannot touch the Q3 numbers. On the same day MPCM noted the Netherlands chose two FFG platforms (ACSV, Wisent 2). Management commentary on the call can unwind a sell-off that rests on a target not yet owned.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on FFG commentary. The deal announcement week (July 2026) and the EGM approval (+11.2% on 2026-08-25) show this stock moves hard on FFG news.
findings.original_quote: Bei FFG droht dem Bericht zufolge rund 150 Beschäftigten Kurzarbeit, falls der Teilezufluss nicht binnen zwei Wochen wieder anläuft. In English: according to the report, about 150 FFG employees face short-time work if the supply of parts does not resume within two weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: The negative half is priced in the 30 Oct move. The release adds the company's account of FFG closing and operations, which is not public. If the market believed the issue was contained, the 30 Oct loss would have been recovered; it has only partly been (9.44 to 9.78).

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is +2.9 (short-squeeze component, 4.31% short, slightly building) and the 20-day run-up is -11.7%. My mild negative cuts against the lean and agrees with the run-up, so p_up is held near 50.
language_note: The Handelsblatt job-cut report (up to 400 posts, small engines, Cologne) and the spokesman's confirmation reached me only through German financial copy (finanztrends, kapitalmarktexperten); no English source carried it.
The WirtschaftsWoche report on the Bundeswehr ZEBEL spare-parts failure and a possible 150-person Kurzarbeit at FFG, the likely trigger of the 30 Oct -7.1% day, was German-only.
German previews carried the Warburg/MPCM view (strong Q3 orders, subdued engine output, targets of EUR 19) and Bernstein's EUR 12.40 reaffirmation; no English preview was found.
The FactSet consensus (Q3 revenue EUR 560m, FY EUR 2,399m) came from finanzen.net's German estimates page.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide': the revenue-guide finding goes from -1.2 to -1.3. It stays capped because the consensus bar has only one source.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): the FCF finding goes from -0.5 to -0.7 and is now filed on the guidance line.
'Too small about the move' and the guidance-change base rate: abs_move_pct goes from 6.5 to 7.0, in line with the name's observed release-day median of about 5.9% and the 7-9% base.
'Positioning is the thing to beat' (the negative agrees with a 4.3% building short): p_up goes from 46 to 47.
